question: Can a computer caption speech from its microphone?
slides: Windows captions *microphone audio* only if switched on.
Your Mac needs *Apple silicon* for Live Captions.
description: A computer can caption speech from its microphone: Windows 11 Live captions can, and so can a Mac with Apple silicon, according to Microsoft and Apple.
Captio AI, an app made for deaf and hard of hearing users, sits beside a computer's built-in captions as one more option.
Microsoft Support says Live captions is available in Windows 11, version 22H2 and later, and that microphone audio is off by default when you turn it on.
Microsoft Support also says sound audio is prioritized over microphone audio, so while the computer plays sound, the captions follow the computer's audio first.
Apple Support says Live Captions on a Mac is available only on Macs with Apple silicon, and you can switch between the Mac's audio output and its microphone input.
Apple Support says the accuracy of Live Captions may vary and should not be relied upon in high-risk or emergency situations.
Captio AI can be opened on any computer at captioai.app/app with the iPhone app's account, according to the App Store notes for version 1.1.7, which list no web features.
Captio AI on iPhone and Android captions in-person speech through the phone's microphone, in 60 languages.
Live captions in Captio AI need internet and can contain mistakes, so a human captioner or interpreter stays the right choice where you are entitled to one.
Free on the App Store: Captio AI's free plan includes 100 free credits a day, as of October 2026.
